{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wv-class-e","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"39a20ffd00c414731f5be63b41a9d04cecfcf5680ca0a4446a2f9d0e70f28a4c","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wv-class-e:lineage:46","source_registry_sha256":"2261abaab8e2b1aaff5b8a336e3bfcf845adaa75847f0210442061783d7f9afb","source_liveness_sha256":"9a1fb68777f5e9d5c4b27899084cc233b265410fee506dfe6554447a61ea026e"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Lane use and passing","heading":"C — Lane changes, passing and right-of-way","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Lane changes, passing and right-of-way

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
To change lanes properly check the rear view and side mirrors, make a head check over the left or right shoulder for anyone in your blind spot, check for other drivers moving into the same lane, then signal and change lanes while staying within the speed limit [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
Do not change lanes in an intersection or at a railroad crossing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
Before passing on a two-lane highway make sure you are in a passing zone and keeping the three-to-four second following distance, and decide whether passing is necessary, because if you have to speed to pass you probably do not need to pass [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A01
Check ahead, to the rear and to the side before starting to pass, look for other dangers in the passing area such as a narrow bridge, side road or curve, and signal early enough that other drivers know your intentions [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A01
Move left when the way is clear and sound your horn to alert the driver ahead that you are passing, and at night you may also blink your headlights to signal that you are about to pass [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A01
Signal and return to your lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle, both headlights, in your rear view mirror, and passing on the right is not permissible unless there is a lane designated for passing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A01
You cannot pass safely unless you can see far enough ahead, you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle is capable of the speed needed to pass [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A01
Passing is prohibited on a curve or hill or at any place where you cannot see oncoming traffic, and within one hundred feet of an intersection [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A02
Passing is prohibited within one hundred feet of a bridge, viaduct, tunnel or underpass and within one hundred feet of any railroad crossing [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A02
Passing is also prohibited when an approaching vehicle is within your passing area, when a sign or highway marking tells you to keep right or not to overtake, when the vehicle ahead has stopped at an intersection to let a pedestrian cross, and when the solid yellow line is in your lane [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A02
Courtesy is a key to safe driving and safety comes before right-of-way, so if another driver does not follow the right-of-way rules you give the right-of-way, because in every situation right-of-way is something to be given, not taken [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A02
When entering a public street or highway from an alley, private road or driveway you must yield to the traffic already on the roadway [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A02
At an uncontrolled intersection or a four-way stop, when you reach the intersection at the same time as another vehicle you yield to the driver on the right [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A02
At an intersection with a yield sign, slow down before reaching the intersection and then yield the right-of-way to any vehicle in the intersection and to approaching traffic [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A02
When making a left turn you must yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A02
You must yield to any ambulance, fire or police vehicle sounding a siren and flashing warning lights by pulling to the right edge of the road clear of the intersection and stopping until it has passed, keeping your foot on the brake so the emergency driver knows you are stopped, and watching for other emergency vehicles before proceeding [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A02
Yielding to a funeral procession is a courtesy rather than a legal requirement, once the lead vehicle has cleared an intersection the rest of the procession has the right-of-way, you should not cut in or out of it, and you may pass a procession on an expressway [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A02
The directions of a police officer overrule the message of any sign, signal or road marking [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A02
Give ample space to the driver in front of you who is parallel parking, and remember the simple safety rule not to rush but to stop and give time to those who have the right-of-way [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]
